clue.text: Composer facing court judgement

indicators.note: one thing facing another stands in front of it, so the composer comes first in the line

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A composer standing in the dock awaits the court's decision on his case.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's formal decision at the end of a trial is a judgement on the case.

clue.text: Struggle to eat animal product? This person may well

definitions.text: Struggle to eat animal product? This person may well

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the first word swallows the second

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
an egg comes from an animal, a hen

explanation.surface: A vegetarian might well find it hard to eat animal produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the first half; the whole clue then describes the answer, who might indeed struggle to eat such things.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian, informally called this, avoids meat and may balk at eating animal produce.

clue.text: Deny match official gets uniform tailor-made on vacation

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, officiates a match
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside of the word is cleared and only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of tailor-made

explanation.surface: A referee rejects the idea that his kit was custom-made while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' suggests a holiday; it means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to prove or declare it false, so the two words mean contradict.

clue.text: Current church stories incorporating popular text? They're for suckers

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so the text goes inside the stories

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
CE is the Church of England
LOL, laugh out loud, is a popular text abbreviation
lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Church gossip spread by text, the kind only gullible people fall for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suckers' suggests gullible people; it means those who suck lollies.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen treats on sticks are licked and sucked, so they are made for people who suck them.

clue.text: 23 Down after breaking bones

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 23 Down

explanation.surface: Someone up and about after breaking a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsal bones form the ankle and back of the foot, a group of small bones.

clue.text: Dismiss article about end of Bram Stoker

indicators.note: the article goes round, about, the single letter taken from the name

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
the indefinite article

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of Bram is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Bram

explanation.surface: Seems to describe sacking a journalist over a piece on the author of Dracula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bram Stoker' reads as the Dracula author, but the name is split: Bram feeds the wordplay and Stoker alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker shovels coal into the furnace of a steam engine, a job also called fireman on the railways.

clue.text: Creatures I filmed at sea, outwardly cute

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of cute

explanation.surface: A wildlife filmmaker recalls shooting adorable animals on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rodents living in meadows and hedgerows are animals, so they are living beings.

clue.text: Discovered thieves cheat

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover removed, so the outside letters are stripped away

parts.note: crooks are thieves or criminals

explanation.surface: Thieves have been found out cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but it means uncovered, with the outer letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is an old slang verb for swindling or overcharging them.

clue.text: Attractive publication with new name that's revolutionary

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so that word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: An appealing magazine with a radical new title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' looks like a noun, a title, but it is the verb meaning to mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic people draw others to them, so the word means charming and alluring as well as pulling iron.

clue.text: Era Einstein transformed

indicators.note: transformed means changed in shape, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Einstein's work changed a whole age of science.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade from 1990 to 1999, or any similar ten-year span, is a period of history.

clue.text: Manager almost makes blunder

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or football manager

explanation.surface: A football manager commits an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a gaffer is an informal word for the boss, especially a football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social slip or embarrassing mistake, which is exactly a blunder.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument Harry groaned on about

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry moaned on and on about a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a person's name, but it is the verb meaning to harass, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-style instrument played from a keyboard, producing sound from vibrating reeds rather than pipes.

clue.text: Keen on purchasing wife objects, unable to decide exactly what

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the first word holds the wife inside it

parts.note: being into something means being keen on it
W is the abbreviation for wife
to mind is to object, as in 'I don't mind'

explanation.surface: Someone keen on buying their wife some objects, but unsure exactly what to get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' reads as a noun, things to buy, but it is the verb meaning to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in two minds is an idiom for hesitating between options, undecided and wavering.

clue.text: Labour's leader ignored reports going round constituency

indicators.note: going round suggests turning back on itself, so the remaining letters are read backwards
something ignored is left out, so that single letter is removed

parts.note: tales are stories or reports

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the party's name is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Political chatter: the Labour leader ignores rumours circulating in a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat in Parliament is the electoral district a member represents, so the two words are synonyms in politics.

clue.text: Dance centre in Macclesfield Bobby maybe acquires

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so the surname holds the middle letters

parts.note: Sir Bobby Charlton, the England and Manchester United footballer

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so just the two central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of Macclesfield

explanation.surface: A footballer named Bobby acquires a dance hall in a Cheshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Charlton was a 1966 World Cup winner; Macclesfield is a town in Cheshire, near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after a city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Take unnecessary risks in stage production of The Towering Inferno?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for courting danger

definitions.text: stage production of The Towering Inferno
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a stage show about a blazing building would be a drama with flames in it

explanation.walkthrough: The Towering Inferno is a 1974 disaster film about a skyscraper fire; staging it would be, literally, a theatrical piece featuring a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting recklessly; read literally, the words describe a theatre drama involving flames.

clue.text: Fancies having variable income

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic variable
earnings are income

explanation.surface: Someone wishes for a pay packet that changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancies' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun: wishes or desires.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearnings are strong desires or longings, so they are fancies in the sense of wishes.

clue.text: Spies entertaining author heading off for tests

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the spies hold the other word

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: heading off means losing its head, so the first letter is cut

parts.note: an author is a writer

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents host a novelist who then departs for some exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards against which things are judged, so they serve as tests or benchmarks.

clue.text: One used to strain, fellow parachutist?

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-pilot
a parachutist is one who lands

explanation.surface: A tired skydiver's companion, straining with the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests effort; in the kitchen it means draining liquid away.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl for draining pasta or vegetables, a kitchen sieve.

clue.text: Rejoin radio broadcast outside English city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, around, the single letter for English
to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An instruction to tune back in to a radio broadcast from outside England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' sits naturally next to radio, but here it is the signal to scramble the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian city, the country's former capital.

clue.text: Virulent illness constricts pulse

indicators.note: to constrict is to squeeze tight, so the words grip the answer within them

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A severe illness slows the heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' reads as a heartbeat; it means an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, such as beans, peas and lentils.

clue.text: Reconciled with daughter, made up for deficiencies

parts.note: at one means in harmony, reconciled
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent, reconciled with their daughter, made amends for past failings.
explanation.walkthrough: The original sense of atone is to be at one, so 'reconciled' gives AT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, compensating for wrongs or shortcomings.

clue.text: Asian band we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is what is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a tie is a band or strip used for fastening

explanation.surface: Seems to report a band from Asia that people are talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group, but here it is a tie, a strip that binds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is a Thai, a nationality in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Fight in such a ring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military battle or clash

definitions.note: the answer is the word that describes such a ring, used attributively
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the kind of ring given when a couple agrees to marry

explanation.surface: A boxer fighting in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring suggests boxing, but it is the ring a fiancée wears.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a battle between armed forces, and an engagement ring marks a promise to marry.

clue.text: Welcoming star not half look excited

indicators.note: welcoming a visitor means taking them in, so the look surrounds the shortened star

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

indicators.note: not half means losing half, so two of the four letters go

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone greeting a celebrity really does look thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is British slang for very much, but here it literally halves star.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means stirring with excitement, in a state of bustle and activity.

clue.text: Tory down in the dumps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the colour of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The party colour stands for a Conservative, and feeling this colour is an idiom for sadness.

clue.text: Mars bar one rogue tried to pinch even

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so the rearranged letters hold the other word between them
a rogue element goes astray, so the remaining letters are disordered
bar here means except, so the word loses the letter for one

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
plane means flat or level, that is, even

explanation.surface: A rascal tried to steal a Mars bar, even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars bar' reads as the chocolate; split, Mars is the definition and bar means without.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is nicknamed for its rusty reddish colour, the fourth world from the Sun.

clue.text: Giant bird some detailed

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A huge bird described in some detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'detailed' as de-tailed: the word loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so the word now names any huge person or thing.

clue.text: Cockney's bald and stuffy

indicators.note: Londoners with a Cockney accent drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: having no hair

explanation.surface: A bald East Ender in a stuffy room.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, famous for dropping the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh ventilation, so it is without moving air, close and oppressive.

clue.text: Runs joint fund, ultimately becoming embittered

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the ankle is a joint of the leg

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of fund

explanation.surface: Someone running a shared fund ends up bitter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint fund' looks like one phrase, but joint and fund are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled caused lasting resentment, leaving a person bitter and sore.
